pos.personaBrief: Valencia and Liverpool were compact 4-2-3-1 sides that pressed and broke quickly (Bleacher Report, LFChistory), with a more attacking style than Cuper's. Control came from organisation and midfield, not possession for its own sake.

pro.personaBrief: Coach Watch says he wants direct, quick attacks after regains, built methodically around first and second balls; the double pivot was a safe holding pair.

est.personaBrief: His teams were built from the back with defined roles, a double pivot and a lone striker; the central midfielders maintain shape (Coach Watch). Wingers worked in both transitions.

lar.personaBrief: 4-2-3-1 with wingers who supported attacks, attacking full-backs and Gerrard central behind Torres; central compactness was prized. He used both wide and inside channels.

blo.personaBrief: LFChistory describes his pressing game as winning the ball high, with Torres defending from the front; Valencia pressed too. Not a low block.

mar.personaBrief: Defended zonal marking at set pieces for five years, said man marking concedes many goals (The National, Irish Times); zonal in open play too.

pla.personaBrief: Opposition-specific preparation in depth (Coach Watch), travelled to watch opponents, changed shape vs Milan with three at the back and Hamann to control Kaka; yet had a fixed method he brought to clubs.

res.personaBrief: A results-driven, defensive-organisation-first manager who rates defence the game's most important facet and saw rotation as the way to win titles.

sis.personaBrief: Obsessive methodical trainer, no luxury players who do not defend, rotation, and fitting players to roles; system over individuals.

jog.personaBrief: Signed more physical players for the Premiership, but also technical pivots like Alonso and Albelda; intensity and organisation prized over classic number 10s.

bas.personaBrief: Built through signings, many Spanish (Garcia, Alonso, Torres, Mascherano, Mista); youngsters used only when needed in his first season, with squad rotation.

lid.personaBrief: Disciplinarian keeping distance from players, banning paella, dropping those not with him; yet explained rotation and calmed players at Istanbul.
